scale.source: CLDR RBNF pl renders 10^9 as "miliard" and 10^12 as "bilion": Polish counts in the long scale. Wiktionary (en), "bilion": "trillion", 10^12.

group_mark.source: CLDR common/main/pl.xml (unicode-org/cldr c0b65ae), number symbols: the group symbol is U+00A0, a no-break space. No dot groups digits.

decimal_mark.source: CLDR common/main/pl.xml (unicode-org/cldr c0b65ae), number symbols: the decimal symbol is a comma.

space_groups.source: CLDR common/main/pl.xml (unicode-org/cldr c0b65ae), number symbols: the group symbol is a no-break space, so groups of three digits after a space are one number.

plural_scale_needs_count.source: CLDR RBNF pl writes a plural scale word only after its count ("dwa tysiące", 2000). A plural scale word with no count names an amount, not a number. Wiktionary (en), "tuzin": also "a large number".

scale_noun_agrees.source: CLDR RBNF pl %spellout-cardinal-masculine renders 10^6, 2 x 10^6, 5 x 10^6 and 21 x 10^6 as "milion", "dwa miliony", "pięć milionów", "dwadzieścia jeden milionów": the scale noun takes the number and case its count governs. The scale words of this lexicon are scale_numeral entries whose plural flag carries that agreement.

joiner_tens_units.source: CLDR RBNF pl renders 21 as "dwadzieścia jeden", no conjunction between tens and units.

joiner_after_hundred.source: CLDR RBNF pl: "100: sto[ >>];", no conjunction after the hundreds.

joiner_between_groups.source: CLDR RBNF pl renders 1001 as "tysiąc jeden", no conjunction between groups.

joiner_before_round_hundred.source: CLDR RBNF pl renders 1100 as "tysiąc sto" and 1500 as "tysiąc pięćset": no joiner stands before a round hundred after the thousands.

hundred_counts_below_thousand.source: unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 (CLDR RBNF pl data), %spellout-cardinal, rendering of 2100: "dwa tysiące sto": the hundred after the thousands is the next group, so a hundred multiplier takes no count of a thousand or more.

compound_parts_by_role.source: compound_words is true, with the source quoted there: the compound number words it cites join cardinal and ordinal words and joiners only, so a fraction noun or a collective is no part of one ("petin|dvajset" is no split).

comma_between_classes.source: CLDR RBNF pl writes no comma between two classes (1001, 1100 and 1500 in the joiner settings above). No source opened shows a comma between two classes of one number, so a comma ends a number.

joiner_before_last_group.source: CLDR RBNF pl renders 1001 as "tysiąc jeden": no conjunction stands before the last group.

ordinal_style.source: CLDR RBNF pl renders 2023 in %spellout-ordinal-masculine as "dwa tysiące dwudziesty trzeci": the thousands stay cardinal and every word after them is ordinal.

compound_words.source: CLDR RBNF pl writes 2000th as one word ("dwutysięczny"). A word that is a sequence of number words reads as its parts.

bare_noun_counts_one.source: Polish has no article, so a singular collective or fraction noun alone counts one. Wiktionary (en), "tuzin": "dozen"; Wiktionary (en), "ćwierć": "quarter".

decimal_fractions.source: CLDR RBNF pl reads the decimals after "przecinek" as a cardinal ("dwa przecinek pięć"); this lexicon has no read source for a power-of-ten fraction after a decimal marker.

ordinal_form_part_takes_no_digits.source: Maintainer ruling on numtag issue 98 for ru, uk and pl, after Д. Э. Розенталь, "Справочник по правописанию и литературной правке", 4th edition (1985), § 45, item 3: "Дробные числительные пишутся раздельно, например: две пятых (2/5)". A fraction in digits is written with a slash, so digits before a part word that is also a plural ordinal form count things: "3 пятых класса" is three fifth-grade classes. The pl plural part word is the plural ordinal form too ("piąte"), so "3 piąte klasy" is three fifth-grade classes.

joiner.source: Wiktionary (en), "pół" gives the half; "i" joins a half to a whole: a paraphrase, the usage example is not on that page.

minus_idioms.source: This lexicon lists no Polish idiom that puts "minus" before a positive number.

negative_particle.source: Wiktionary, "ani", Polish particle: "nary, not a, not even one", "Nie było ani jednego ciasteczka." (There wasn't even a single cookie.) After "ani" the word for one counts nothing.

number_name.source: Słownik synonimów PWN, "jeden i ten sam": "ten sam", "jedno i to samo"; Korpus języka polskiego: "był to często jeden i ten sam człowiek". The set phrase means "the same" and counts nothing. The list holds its case forms in each gender and the plural.

article_one.source: Polish has no article; "jeden" is a numeral.

of.source: Polish marks the counted noun by case, with no "of" word.

fraction_of.source: Polish marks the counted noun by case, with no "of" word.

denominator_particle.source: Polish has no particle like Portuguese "avos".

class_noun.source: Polish names no digit class with a singular noun after a collective.

half_unit.source: Wiktionary (en), "pół": "half", one of two: the half is its own word before the unit, read by the half role.

abbreviation.source: No Polish number word in this lexicon is also an abbreviation with a period.

lone_decimal_mark.source: CLDR common/main/pl.xml (unicode-org/cldr c0b65ae): the decimal symbol is a comma; a comma before the first digit marks decimals.

Jagodziński, «Tworzenie i składnia liczebników» (Papers/Languages/Slavic/Polish/jagodzinski-liczebniki.html): "z dwoma trzecimi bochenka, w jednej czwartej miast", "trzy czwarte pizzy": the numerator is a feminine cardinal and the part a feminine ordinal; after 2, 3 or 4 the part is a nominative plural ("trzy czwarte"). SILVER: after 5 or more, and after a count that ends in 1 above 1, the part is a genitive plural ("pięć ósmych"), by the agreement rule of 5 and more; no saved example.
